release_tag.description: The tag put on the submitted commit.

notion_member.description: Whether EX-DEVB-CHECK requires dev B's Notion token check.

validator_globs.description: Comma-separated globs of the validator/contract sources frozen by EX-FREEZE-VALIDATOR.

recording_globs.description: Comma-separated globs frozen for the recording (EX-FREEZE-RECORDING).

docs_globs.description: Comma-separated globs frozen by the docs freeze (EX-FREEZE-DOCS).

item.description: Per-item templates: a short name of the item (contract item, fix item).

item_writes.description: Per-item templates: the glob the item's task writes.

test_cmd.description: Per-item templates: the proof command (bash, from the repository root).

deploy_url.description: EX-DEPLOY: the URL that must answer 200 after the deploy.

evidence_path.description: EX-EVID: the repository-relative file the evidence capture writes.

fix_file.description: EX-FIX-CODE: the file (or glob) the fix changes.

revert_sha.description: EX-FIX-REVERT: the full SHA of the commit to revert.

revert_files.description: EX-FIX-REVERT: the files (glob) the reverted commit touched.

devb_task.description: EX-DEVB-INTEGRATE: the T-id of dev B's manual task whose branch is integrated.

templates.title: Bootstrap the product repository
templates.description: Bootstrap the product repository on branch main: write .gitattributes with the line '* text=auto eol=lf', commit the portable commit-msg hook that exec.py init wrote at .githooks/commit-msg (executable bit through git update-index --chmod=+x) so every clone refuses an AI-attribution trailer and a non-conventional header, and check core.longpaths. Commit with git commit -F from a message file.

nfr.title: Repository bootstrapped with portable guards and CI
nfr.text: The product repository has LF line endings, the portable commit-msg hook refusing AI trailers and non-conventional headers, and a CI workflow running the offline gates.

spec.cmd:
grep -qxF '* text=auto eol=lf' .gitattributes && git ls-files -s .githooks/commit-msg | grep -q '^100755' && f=$(mktemp) && printf 'feat: x

Co-''Authored-By: X <x@example.invalid>
' > "$f" && ! sh .githooks/commit-msg "$f" && printf 'update x
' > "$f" && ! sh .githooks/commit-msg "$f" && printf 'feat: add x
' > "$f" && sh .githooks/commit-msg "$f"

expect.summary: LF attributes set; the tracked executable hook refuses a trailer and a non-conventional header and accepts a conventional one

negative_control.description: on the commit before the bootstrap, .gitattributes or the hook is absent: the proof fails

steps: Install Claude Code at the version dev A runs (claude --version, at least 2.1.286), set DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 as a user environment variable, and log in.
Install Python 3.11 or newer (as python), Node 20 or newer, pnpm 10, git and gh; run gh auth login.
Copy the four skill folders dev A sends you into ~/.claude/skills/ (execution, frontend, harden, hackathon) and the global guard into ~/.claude/hooks/ (guard.py, py.sh) with its settings entry.
Accept the GitHub invitations to the product repository and the private state repository.
Accept the Notion workspace invitation as a member (not a guest), then connect the Notion connector in claude.ai.

Clone the product repository, cd into it, then run python ~/.claude/skills/execution/scripts/exec.py init --project {project} --executor B --state-remote <state repo url> and python ~/.claude/skills/execution/scripts/exec.py agents install.
Start the launcher from the repository root (~/.claude/skills/execution/assets/launcher/launch-exec.ps1 or .sh) and type /execution.
Reply « prêt » with the state repo commit SHA your orchestrator printed after its first sync.
